text:
Jared Spurgeon is 36, has played 1,028 games for Minnesota, and is having a better season than last. He has nine points in 16 games, and the Wild take 61% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on (expected goals measure the quality of chances), ten points better than without him.

Some of that is luck: Minnesota has scored about 8.4 more goals than its chances with him on the ice, a lot for a defenseman who plays 20 minutes, and his points pace is far above his talent range. The defense is the real part. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 93rd percentile at taking chances away last season even as his overall value dipped to replacement level. He scored the 2-1 goal in Vancouver on Saturday, 1:12 after the Canucks had scored. With Quinn Hughes out, Spurgeon's minutes may matter more. Our range has him around 28 points.
